---
title: "Activation atlas"
subtitle: "What two kraken line recognisers compute, frame by frame, with the controls that decide what it means"
toc: false
---

The atlas reads the activations of two kraken models: one for nineteenth-century German Kurrent
(`kraken-german-xix-blb-v1`) and one for the Bern Hertwig hand (`kraken-bern-hertwig-v2`). It asks
which part of the line each block depends on, what its units and directions encode, and what breaks when they
are switched off. Each result is shown next to its controls: a randomly initialised network, shuffled
lines and, for the Bern model, seed runs fine-tuned from the same parent.

The explorer below shows six practice lines per model. A cursor moves along the line; for the frame
under it the page shows every unit of every block, the five most probable output characters, and
which part of the line the selected block depends on. Click a block or a unit for its results, each
with its verdict. The view is kept in the link, so a link opens the same line, frame and unit.

::: {.callout-note title="What the atlas does not show"}
Both gates of the atlas failed, and the page shows them as banners. **Gate 1:** occlusion places a
letter to within one neighbour, not on the letter itself, so the explorer shows activation, not
location; the character row under the line is the CTC alignment, drawn for reading. **Gate 2:** no
single unit is selective beyond the random network's best unit, so the atlas is descriptive and the
ablation groups are shown as descriptions, not as circuits.
:::

The twelve line images are practice lines, not held-out data. They are crops of archival scans and keep the licences of their owners; they are not covered by the site's CC BY 4.0. The atlas is built from the repository
with `python -m wsp.atlas` and `python -m wsp.atlas_explore`; the full report is
[`docs/ATLAS_REPORT.md`](https://github.com/thodel/weightspace/blob/main/docs/ATLAS_REPORT.md).
